what_happened: Two source files grew very large: gh.rs reached 5,276 lines and run.rs's produce_and_verify reached 724 lines. Both changed in about 10 landings in one week and were where that week's breakages happened. Nobody on the system noticed. Sri had to ask about code quality himself. His earlier request of 2026-10-17 (20261017-205558-dn2e) to reconsider the design every few jobs was never run, because the planning brain kept ranking other work above it.
cause: Recurring work such as a design or code-health review is treated as an ordinary queue item that competes for rank with feature work, and always loses. No stage owns code health, and nothing measures file size, function length or churn against limits that would queue work on their own. Detection therefore depends on the owner noticing.
prevention: A standing code-health check, in Hestia's scope, that runs on a fixed cadence (for example every N landings) and is not ranked against other work. It measures file length, function length and per-file landing churn against configured thresholds. When a threshold is crossed it queues a refactor or design-review job itself, and it records the breach. Starting values: files over about 1,500 lines, functions over about 150 lines, and a file touched by more than 5 landings in a week. The 2026-10-17 periodic design review request becomes this scheduled review rather than a rankable item.
proposed_request: Add a standing code-health check to Athena, in Hestia's scope. Outcome: oversized or fast-changing code is found and queued for work automatically, without the owner asking, and the periodic design review requested on 2026-10-17 (20261017-205558-dn2e) runs on its own cadence. Acceptance: (1) Thresholds for file length, function length and per-file landing count in a rolling week are set in athena.toml, with the config schema updated in the same change. Starting values are 1,500 lines per file, 150 lines per function, and 5 landings per file per week. (2) The check runs after every N landings (N configurable, default 10) and is not ranked against other queue items. (3) When a threshold is crossed it queues a refactor or design-review job naming the file or function and the measured value, and it queues no duplicate while one is open. (4) A test runs the check on a fixture with a file over the limit and a function over the limit, and shows two jobs queued. A second run shows no duplicates. A clean fixture queues nothing. (5) Run on the current repo, it reports gh.rs and produce_and_verify as breaches. (6) The 20261017-205558-dn2e request is marked as satisfied by this scheduled review. Do not split gh.rs or run.rs in this job. Add a changelog entry in the default form.
